title: Operational Rotas and Skill Lattice for Model-Serving Incident Ops
author: Lena Alvarez
content:
Overview:

This handbook defines a practical on-call rota structure and a skill-lattice (competency map) tailored for incident response in Redwood's model-serving platform. The goal is to reduce time-to-recovery for user-visible degradations while building a repeatable training pipeline (game-days, mentorship, and assessment) that grows responder capability across teams.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments that use the model-serving runtime (service names: runtime-gateway, kv-proxy, batch-router, inference-worker).
- Covers first 60 minutes of incident lifecycle (rapid triage + stabilization), escalation criteria for multi-region failover, and a 90-day skill progression plan.

Key SLOs and thresholds (for incident automation and routing):
- API p99 latency (end-to-end): 250ms target; SLO alert threshold: >350ms for 5m across 3 hosts.
- Token-generation error rate: 0.1% target; alert at 0.5% over 10m.
- Model-quality regressions (based on eval sentinel tests): immediate paging when regressions exceed 10% of baseline on golden prompt set.

Roles & responsibilities:
- First Responder (FR): triage, evidence capture, immediate mitigations (circuit breakers, traffic limiting). Owner: on-call engineer.
- Bridge Operator (BO): open/operate the incident bridge, coordinate cross-team work, public status updates. Owner: SRE on rotation.
- Service Owner (SO): deep debugging, patch development, redeploy coordination. Owner: owning service team.
- Contingency Lead (CL): decides fallbacks (model variant routing, region failover, capacity reallocation) and approves customer comms. Owner: senior SRE / platform engineer.

Rota structure (practical pattern used across teams):
1) Primary on-call (FR) — 1 week cadence, 7x24 responsibility for immediate triage and short mitigations.
2) Secondary on-call (BO) — 1 week cadence, overlap hours 08:00–18:00 local for handovers and escalations.
3) Tertiary / Pager escalation pool — senior engineers paged for high-severity. Rotation: 2-week blocks.
4) Skill mentor pairing — new responders are paired with a senior mentor for first two rotations.

Skill lattice (competency map) — concise levels and required capabilities:
- Level 1 (Observer): can use dashboards, acknowledge pages, read runbook checklists, reproduce simple latency spikes in staging.
- Level 2 (Responder): run triage runloop, collect KV cache snapshots, rotate traffic, create bridge notes.
- Level 3 (Troubleshooter): interpret perf profiles (nvprof/trace), apply kernel-level workarounds, coordinate model rollbacks.
- Level 4 (Contingency Lead): authorize region failovers, design cross-service mitigation plans, and sign off customer communications.

Assessment checklist (promotes between levels):
- Demonstrated runbook execution in two game-days (recorded).
- One on-call shift with mentor sign-off (for Levels 2+).
- Troubleshoot a synthetic degradation in staging within SLA during simulation (for Level 3).

Training & game-day curriculum (12-week cycle):
- Week 1: Orientation — runbook walkthroughs, bridge tooling, status page update templates.
- Week 2–3: Tabletop drills — service dependency mapping and escalation exercises.
- Week 4: Live simulation 1 — KV cache leak and slow IO (FR executes stabilization steps).
- Week 6: Live simulation 2 — model quality regression triggered by bad weights; practice model-rollout rollback.
- Week 8: Cross-team swarm — SRE + Platform + Applied ML practice coordinated containment.
- Week 12: Certification run — full incident run (10-minute triage + 60-minute remediation) graded against a rubric.

Incident triage runloop (first 10 minutes — "Rapid Restoration Loop"):
1) Acknowledge page and open incident bridge.
2) Determine blast radius: services, customers, regions.
3) Capture quick evidence: p99/p50, error logs (last 10m), recent deploys, model version mappings.
4) Apply one immediate mitigation (rate-limiter, reduce concurrency, fallback model).
5) Update status page and raise escalation if mitigation fails in 8 minutes.

Runbook snippet: KV-cache high-miss spike
- Symptoms: sudden p50→p95 increase, kv-proxy miss ratio > 40%, eviction rate spikes.
- Immediate actions (FR):
  1) Check kv-proxy metrics (path: /dashboards/kv-proxy:miss-rate).
  2) Capture cache keys hot list: curl -s http://kv-proxy/metrics/hot-keys | jq -r '.keys[0:50]'.
  3) Temporarily increase cache throttle threshold: kubectl -n runtime patch configmap kv-proxy-cfg --patch '{"data": {"throttle": "1.2"}}'.
  4) If miss rate still > 30% after 5m, route 10% traffic to model-variant quantized-v1 (runtime-gateway policy: variant=quant-v1).
  5) Call SO and BO; prepare rollback plan.

Escalation matrix (simplified):
- Sev 1 (global outage): notify CL + entire tertiary pool, consider multi-region failover.
- Sev 2 (partial outage/many customers): notify BO + SO, prepare customer impact statement.
- Sev 3 (single-customer or cosmetic): FR owns containment and patch path.

Status page mapping and customer comms templates:
- Status taxonomy: operational / degraded / partial outage / major outage.
- Map technical state -> customer message (short template):
  - Title: "Partial degradation of Redwood inference in us-west-2"
  - Body: "We are investigating increased latency affecting text-generation requests in us-west-2. Our on-call team has applied temporary traffic limiting and is routing traffic to unaffected nodes while we investigate. Expected next update: 20 minutes. If your applications are impacted, contact support@redwood.ai with incident ID INC-YYYYMMDD-####."
- Public status cadence: initial, 20m, 60m, 3hr, and resolution. Include "what we're doing" and "workaround if any" sections.

Operational metrics to capture during incidents (minimum):
- Time to Acknowledge (TTA), Time to First Mitigation (TTM), Time to Restore (TTR).
- Evidence bucket: list of logs (samplenames), perf profiles, kv snapshots, model version diffs.

Runbook ownership and maintenance:
- Each runbook document must have an owning service and a runbook-owner tag in the docs repo. Review cadence: quarterly for critical runbooks, annual for lower-severity ones.
- Post-incident: FR creates a short incident note in the bridge, SO drafts a technical postmortem; the CL assigns action items and due dates.

Appendix: example CLI & JSON snippets
- Bridge creation (CLI):
  /tools/bridge create --title "INC: model-quality-regression" --severity 2 --owner lena.alvarez@redwood.ai

- Example routing policy JSON (used to shift 10% traffic):
  {
    "policy": "weighted-routing",
    "from": "runtime-gateway:us-west-2",
    "to": [{"variant": "quant-v1", "weight": 10}, {"variant": "baseline", "weight": 90}]
  }

Appendix: Post-incident learning & certification pattern:
- Within 7 days: FR and SO submit a timeline and evidence artifacts.
- Within 14 days: CL assigns follow-ups, game-day replay scheduled within next cycle.
- Certification: engineers who complete the curriculum and two graded simulations are promoted along the lattice.

Ownership matrix (example table described):
- runtime-gateway: owner-team runtime-team@redwood.ai, runbook-owner: mariam.kim@redwood.ai
- kv-proxy: owner-team infra-team@redwood.ai, runbook-owner: marcus.chen@redwood.ai

This document is intended to be prescriptive for operational teams and flexible enough to be used in enterprise Private deployments with minor configuration changes. Review questions or suggestions to the SRE training mailbox: sre-training@redwood.ai.
